subject: Re: RFI - GPU slotting & throughput plan for Hypernova AI
messages:
From: Lara Chen <lara.chen@hypernova.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurements@hypernova.ai
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: RFI: GPU slotting, quantization profiles, and burst planning for Hypernova inference

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for taking our RFI. A few clarifying items up front so our procurement and infra teams can map to TCO:

- We expect an initial production baseline of ~200 QPS (request-level) for generation workloads, ~1.2B tokens/day, with weekly peak bursts up to 3x baseline during marketing pushes.
- Primary models: conversational 30B LM (long context up to 8k tokens) and a 7B summarization model used in batch.
- Key asks in the RFI: GPU family recommendations by SLA tier, expected tokens/sec and p95 latency per GPU class, recommended quantization levels with observed quality delta, and how reservations + burst lanes are modeled in billing.

Please attach any benchmark matrices, quantization guidance, and a rough reservation sizing worksheet (we'd like to see a couple of scenario buckets: conservative, expected, aggressive). Also flag any gotchas for multi-region fallbacks.

Attached is our short RFI template (single-sheet) — let me know if you need a 30m slideover this week.

Appreciate it,
Lara
Procurement Program Manager
Hypernova AI

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: RFI: GPU slotting, quantization profiles, and burst planning for Hypernova inference

Hi Lara — thanks for the clear ask and the template.

We put together an initial sizing and guidance pack and attached three artifacts: 1) GPU slotting + throughput matrix, 2) quantization profiles summary, 3) a short reservation/ burst pricing explainer. High level callouts below; detailed numbers are in the spreadsheet.

High-level recommendation (three buckets):
- Conservative: 8 x A100-80GB slots (good for cost-sensitive batch + small-scale real-time); expected steady throughput ~5k tokens/sec aggregate, p95 latency ~220-350ms for 30B at 2-token batching.
- Expected (recommended): 4 x H100-80GB + 6 x A100-80GB mix. H100 handles sustained low-latency 30B traffic; A100s provide cheaper capacity for background batch and summarization. Aggregate steady throughput ~20k tokens/sec, p95 latency ~90-160ms on H100 for 30B with 4-8 token batching.
- Aggressive / burst-ready: add 2 x H100 burst lanes (on reserved burst pool) and enable mixed-precision int8 quant for the 7B and summarize model. This gives ~3x headroom during marketing spikes.

Quantization guidance:
- 7B summarizer: int4 / int8 best-in-class with negligible quality delta; recommend int4 for cost-sensitive batch runs.
- 30B conv: we recommend int8 with a validation prompt set; int4 will reduce latency/cost but may need prompt-specific evals for conversational fidelity.

Reservation & billing notes (summary):
- Reserved slots = lower unit cost + guaranteed capacity; burst lanes = pre-provisioned transient capacity charged at a blended premium (30–50% on top of reserved rate) only when used.
- Fallback policy: when capacity exhausted we route to lower-cost A100 quantized variants with a configurable latency/cost SLO.

Next steps: can we schedule 30 minutes Wednesday 11/11 to walk the spreadsheet? If that works, we'll bring Karthik for quantization profiles and Grace to cover SLAs/rollback policies.

Attached: Redwood_RFI_GPU-Matrix.xlsx, quant_profiles_summary.pdf, SLA_Addendum_Redwood.docx

Best,
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales – Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 06 Nov 2026 11:26:00 -0800
Subject: RE: RFI: GPU slotting & quantization notes (internal)

Jordan / Grace — quick internal note to calibrate math before the call:

- The H100 throughput numbers in the sheet assume the updated kernel set (attention & kv-cache optimizations) and 4-token microbatching for interactive loads. If Hypernova wants 1-token tail-latency SLOs we'll need +30% baseline headroom.
- For mixed load (30B conv + 7B batch) the recommended packing is to map the majority of long-context conv sessions to H100 and route summarize/batch to A100 with heavy prefix caching. That preserves latency while keeping unit cost down.
- Quantization: provide both int8 and int4 artifacts. Run customer-specific evals on a 200-prompt set. Add a short note about hallucination risk when moving 30B to int4 and suggested mitigations (temperature capping, rerank pass).

I'll prepare the small eval-runner snippet for their team and include example eval prompts in the shared drive.

Karthik
Applied ML – Redwood Inference
From: Samuel Ortiz <samuel.ortiz@hypernova.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lara Chen <lara.chen@hypernova.ai>, procurements@hypernova.ai
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 09:08:00 -0800
Subject: Question on reservation tiers & burst economics

Jordan — quick question ahead of the call:

1) If we pick the \"Expected\" bucket, how is the blend priced during a burst when we auto-burst to H100 lanes? Do we pay only used burst time (minute-granular) or is there a minimum billing increment?
2) For the fallback to quantized A100 variants, do you charge egress/latency adders? We need to show our FinOps team the worst-case monthly spend.

Also please confirm whether the SLA addendum supports cross-region failover (we want automatic fallback from us-west to us-east).

Thanks — Sam
Infra Lead, Hypernova AI
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Samuel Ortiz <samuel.ortiz@hypernova.ai>, Lara Chen <lara.chen@hypernova.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Question on reservation tiers & burst economics

Sam / Lara — answering inline and consolidating next steps.

1) Burst billing model:
- Bursts are billed by the minute with a 5-minute minimum increment for any burst lane activation. If you configure autoscale burst pools, you only pay for the minutes those GPUs are actively serving. We include a capped 'standby' charge option for guaranteed warm-up (optional).

2) Fallback to quantized A100 variants:
- No separate egress adders beyond standard networking; latency adders are not separately billed — you are billed by token units consumed. The cost delta comes from the lower-cost instance pricing of quantized variants. We'll provide worst-case monthly spend scenarios in the workbook (see the "cost_scenarios" tab).

3) Cross-region failover:
- SLA addendum supports cross-region failover with an opt-in failover pool and documented RTO/RPO targets. Automatic failover increments the applicable rate (we've documented the failover premium in the SLA_Addendum_Redwood.docx).

Action items / next steps:
- Karthik: finalize the 200-prompt eval package and share results link (Jonas to coordinate infra testbed).
- Grace: we will include a short runbook for rollback & fallback thresholds in the proposal.
- Jordan: schedule Wed 11/11 10:00am PT for the 30m walkthrough; will send calendar invite and a one-page exec summary.

I'll also upload a version of the spreadsheet with the two worst-case monthly spend scenarios flagged.

Thanks — talk Wednesday,
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales – Redwood Inference
